item.description: October 19, 2026: referendum formally successful October 6, 2026: 79 479 signatures submitted 78 922 signatures were declared valid LENu amendment
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - October 19, 2026: referendum formally successful - October 6, 2026: 79 479 signatures submitted - 78 922 signatures were declared valid - Amendment to LENu dated June 19, 2026
## Key facts - Publication date → October 19, 2026 - Location → Bern - Submission date → October 6, 2026 - Signatures submitted → 79 479 - Valid signatures → 78 922 - Contested act → amendment to LENu of June 19, 2026 - Outcome → referendum formally successful
In the Federal Chancellery’s press release, published on October 19, 2026, Bern reports the success of the referendum on the amendment to the Federal Act on Nuclear Energy (LENu). The contested text is the amendment to the same Act dated June 19, 2026. The news therefore concerns the formal status of the collection of signatures, not the content of the legislative amendment, which is not described in the press release.
On October 6, 2026, the referendum committee submitted 79 479 signatures. The Federal Chancellery’s verification established that 78 922 of the submitted signatures were valid. Following this finding, the referendum was declared formally successful. The press release does not present this as an outcome on the merits of the amendment: it merely describes the formal success.
### The figure certified by the Federal Chancellery
The passage indicated in the source is the verification of the signatures. The Federal Chancellery does not merely report the total submitted by the committee: it specifies how many signatures are valid and links this verification to the formal success of the referendum. The wording delineates the information available and attests to the formal outcome indicated on October 19, 2026, without presenting a judgment on the content of the amended LENu. There is a difference of 557 signatures between the signatures submitted and those recognized as valid: 79 479 minus 78 922. This is a calculation based on the two figures reported by the source, not an additional figure reported separately. ## The dates distinguish three stages
The three dates in the communiqué do not indicate the same thing. June 19, 2026 identifies the amendment to LENu against which the referendum is directed; October 6, 2026 marks the submission of the signatures by the referendum committee; October 19, 2026 is the date of publication of the announcement from Bern. The sequence therefore sets out in order the contested act, the filing of the signatures, and the communication of the formal outcome.
| Date | Reported element | |---|---| | June 19, 2026 | Amendment to LENu against which the referendum is directed | | October 6, 2026 | Submission of 79 479 signatures by the referendum committee | | October 19, 2026 | Publication of the communiqué and recording of 78 922 valid signatures |
This comparison helps avoid confusing the date of the amendment with that of the announcement. The Federal Chancellery communicated the number of valid signatures within the text published on October 19, while the submission of the signatures took place on October 6. These are distinct stages in the same documentary account: first the amendment is indicated, then the filing, and finally the confirmation of the referendum’s success.
### The comparison that can be made
The source permits a limited chronological and numerical comparison. Chronologically, it links each date to a specific element. Numerically, it provides two different quantities: the signatures submitted and those that were valid. The difference between the two quantities can be seen by comparing 79 479 and 78 922; there is no need to attribute any further meaning to them beyond the validity established by the Federal Chancellery.
The text does not indicate a date for a vote and does not report an outcome on the substance of the amendment. Therefore, the chronology describes the formal status of the referendum as of the publication date, without providing a subsequent timetable. ## The scope of the news
The communiqué makes it possible to establish the formal outcome precisely, but does not broaden the picture beyond the collection and validation of the signatures. For an accurate reading, the source documents that 78 922 of the signatures submitted are valid and that the referendum against the amendment to LENu has formally succeeded. The text also notes the role of the referendum committee, which submitted the signatures on October 6, 2026, but does not state its name.
### Limits indicated by the source
The following remain outside the text: - the content of the amendment of June 19, 2026; - the reasons given by the referendum committee; - further dates or deadlines; - an outcome on the substance of the law.
These limits define the scope of the announcement. The source documents a formal success, not a decision on the substance of the federal law on nuclear energy. It does not attribute statements to the committee, the Federal Chancellery or other parties, and does not describe regulatory consequences. The article can therefore reconstruct who submitted the signatures, how many were recognized as valid, which amendment is being challenged, and when the news was published. It cannot, however, add positions, scenarios or deadlines not contained in the communiqué.

item.title: GLP-1 anti-obesity drugs: impact on the food industry
item.description: In Switzerland, less than 2% are on GLP-1 therapy In the USA, the food budget falls by up to 5% Emmi, Danone and Nestlé adapt their product ranges
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - In Switzerland, less than 2% are undergoing GLP-1 therapy - In the US, food budgets fall by up to 5% - Emmi, Danone and Nestlé adapt their product ranges - Givaudan estimates annual growth of 9%
## Key facts - GLP-1 therapy in Switzerland → below 2% last year - Food budget in the USA → reduction of up to 5% - Growth estimated by Givaudan → around 9% annually over the next five years - Overweight Swiss population → 43% in 2022 - Swiss population meeting obesity criteria → 12% in 2022 - Data on Swiss therapy → analysis by Helsana for AWP
Last year, in Switzerland, the share of the population undergoing treatment with GLP-1 drugs stood below 2%. The figure comes from an analysis conducted by Helsana, the country’s largest health insurer, on behalf of AWP. According to ATS, the percentage remains modest, but over the same number of years it has increased nearly tenfold.
The Keystone-ATS service places this development within a broader transformation of the food industry. The motto Eat less, eat better accompanies new treatments for obesity and overweight and puts pressure on a sector traditionally geared toward immediate gratification.
Théodore Duval-Segard, head of the food sector at AlphaValue, notes that the majority of publicly listed companies in Europe active in the food and beverage sector focus their activities on alcohol, sugar, chocolate and fats. Certified dietitian Natalie Bez, who conducts research at the Bern University of Applied Sciences, likewise believes that these products are ill-advised for the general population and even less suitable for those who want to lose weight.
> According to Duval-Segard, what initially might have seemed like a fad is becoming a structural phenomenon: the spread of GLP-1 therapies and the decline in their prices are prompting food group executives to rethink their product ranges.
The analyst estimates that the share of the stock-market capitalization of the food and beverage industry compatible with GLP-1 does not exceed 10%. Three companies are exceptions, however: Danone, the French giant active in the water and yogurt sectors; Emmi, a dairy company based in Lucerne; and Ebro Foods, a Spanish company specializing in rice and pasta.
For the Swiss companies mentioned, the change concerns not only the volume of food consumed. The source describes a review of product ranges, portions and nutritional profiles, with proteins assigned a central role. The market remains in a different phase from the North American one, where the use of these treatments is already much more widespread. ## The comparison of data and strategies
### Percentages do not measure the same thing
The first comparison requires caution because the available data refer to different measures. In the United States, recent studies have found that households affected by the treatments may reduce their food budget by up to 5%. In Switzerland, by contrast, the figure below 2% indicates the share of the population undergoing GLP-1 therapy last year. The first figure concerns a household's spending; the second measures the prevalence of the treatment in the population.
| Indicator | Area | Value and period | |---|---|---| | Food budget of affected households | United States | Reduction of up to 5% | | Population undergoing GLP-1 therapy | Switzerland | Below 2% last year | | Overweight population | Switzerland | 43% in 2022 | | Population meeting the criteria for obesity | Switzerland | 12% in 2022 |
The 5% is therefore not an estimate of the cost of living in Switzerland and cannot be used to calculate how much Swiss households spend. The source does not provide a national equivalent for the food budget. It does, however, show the direction observed in the United States: fewer snacks and sugary products, more fresh food, smaller portions and protein-rich products.
The composition of the product offering explains why companies start from different positions. Danone and Emmi are identified as the best positioned because of their activities related to milk processing. Emmi's portfolio is already rich in protein and also includes high-end desserts. Duval-Segard attributes a particular positioning to the Lucerne-based company precisely because desserts can preserve moments of pleasure in the diet of patients undergoing GLP-1 therapy.
Nestlé follows a different path. Faced with an issue considered essentially incompatible with its business model, the Vaud-based multinational developed a completely new offering for patients undergoing GLP-1 therapy and introduced it in the United States in 2024. The company is also betting on protein-enriched beverages.
The comparison also concerns ingredient technology. The addition of protein strongly alters the taste and requires reformulation to mask the effect. For this reason, Givaudan, the Geneva-based group known above all for fragrances, identifies an opportunity in the Flavors division. Ebro Foods completes the group of exceptions cited by the analyst, with its specialization in rice and pasta. ## The scope of Swiss data
### Still concentrated in North America
For the time being, the GLP-1 phenomenon is most widespread in North America. Recent observations indicate that these treatments have been prescribed to more than one in ten adults to combat diabetes or overweight. In Switzerland, by contrast, the therapy concerned less than 2% of the population last year, although the share was nearly ten times that of ten years earlier.
The article links the possibility of further growth to the prevalence of overweight among the Swiss population. In 2022, the Federal Statistical Office, FSO, estimated that 43% of people were overweight and 12% met the criteria for obesity. These figures describe the condition of the population, not the number of patients taking GLP-1 drugs. They therefore do not allow a direct forecast of future sales or treatments.
The figure compiled by Helsana also has a precise scope: it measures the population undergoing treatment and does not describe premiums, reimbursements or the rules of LAMal/KVG. The source also does not indicate how many treatments were prescribed for diabetes and how many for overweight in Switzerland. This distinction makes it impossible to turn the growth recorded over ten years into a detailed estimate of the national market.
### Protein, taste and reformulation
From a nutritional perspective, Natalie Bez considers it a priority to ensure sufficient protein intake alongside a balanced diet that includes minerals, vitamins, whole grains, fruit and vegetables. For the industry, increasing protein content is problematic because it can significantly alter the taste of food. According to Duval-Segard, producers must modify product formulations to mitigate this consequence.
Givaudan is trying to turn this difficulty into an opportunity for its Flavours division. This summer, director Antoine Khalil estimated annual growth of around 9% over the next five years for the market he was referring to, adding that the group intends to benefit from it more than proportionally.
Nestlé provides another documented element: the range intended for GLP-1 patients was launched in 2024 in the United States, not in Switzerland. The source provides no data on the Swiss sales of the companies mentioned, market shares, the impact on consumer prices or any new products intended for the national market. The available picture therefore concerns announced strategies, prevalence data and an industry estimate, not a comprehensive forecast for the Swiss economy.

item.description: The opposing committee presented its arguments in Bern The federal vote on the initiative is scheduled for November 29 Individual taxation will enter
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The opposing committee presented its arguments in Bern - The federal vote on the initiative is scheduled for November 29 - Individual taxation will enter into force from 2032 - The opponents' estimate ranges from 700 million to 3 billion annually
## Key facts - Proponent: Il Centro - Opponents: PLR, PS, Verdi, Verdi liberali, business organizations and trade unions - Objective: eliminate the tax discrimination against married couples - Announced model: individual taxation from 2032 - Levels involved: federal, cantonal and municipal - Initiative: direct federal tax only - Planned method: aggregation of spouses' incomes in the tax return - Scenario indicated: up to three income tax returns
### The conference in Bern In Bern, on Monday, the cross-party committee opposed to Il Centro's initiative presented its arguments ahead of the federal vote on November 29. The proposal under discussion aims to eliminate tax discrimination against married couples; the committee, however, considers it unnecessary and too costly.
The coalition brings together representatives of PLR, PS, Verdi and Verdi liberali, as well as business organizations and trade unions. According to the committee, the popular vote last March, which approved the transition to individual taxation, has already removed the marriage penalty.
In August, the government announced that this model would take effect from 2032. The change will affect the three levels of government indicated in the source: federal, cantonal and municipal. For the opponents, the distinction between the model already approved and the initiative now being put to a vote is central.
Il Centro's proposal, in fact, concerns only direct federal tax and provides for the aggregation of spouses' incomes in the tax return. The campaign presented in Bern is therefore based on two verifiable elements: extending the model to the three levels and the initiative's narrower scope, limited to the IFD. The committee also indicates a loss of revenue for the Confederation, ranging from 700 million to 3 billion francs per year. ## The comparison between the two scopes
### A three-level reform and a text limited to IFD The point that emerges from the committee's arguments is a comparison of scope, not a comparison between two tax figures reported in the source. The model of individual taxation is described as a change valid at the federal, cantonal and municipal levels. The Centro initiative, on the other hand, concerns only direct federal tax and provides for adding the spouses' incomes together in the tax return.
| Element | Individual taxation | The Centro initiative | | Scope | Federal, cantonal and municipal | Direct federal tax only | | Status indicated | Approved in a popular vote last March | Ahead of the November 29 vote | | Spouses' incomes | The text does not specify a method here | Aggregation in the tax return |
The table highlights a precise difference: the first model concerns all three levels of government, whereas the Centro proposal operates at only one. The source does not provide tax rates, amounts per family or simulations; therefore, the documented comparison concerns institutional scope and the treatment of incomes in the tax return.
This difference in scope gives rise to the opponents' criticism. If the initiative were accepted, the committee argues that it would create tax chaos with up to three income tax returns. The same argument adds that, even if the yes vote were to prevail, the cantons and municipalities would nevertheless have to introduce individual taxation.
The outcome envisaged by the opponents is therefore a possible coexistence between the aggregation provided for by the initiative for IFD and individual taxation, which would also have to be introduced at cantonal and municipal level. This is the concrete relationship indicated in the source: not a calculation of the benefit for a single couple, but a difference between scope and filing method. ## Benefits, marriage and revenue shortfall
### The «marriage bonus» The opposition's second line of argument concerns the alternative calculation method provided for by the initiative. The committee argues that this method would introduce a «marriage bonus». In the argument presented in Bern, the bonus would have a specific effect: it would once again disadvantage unmarried couples.
The opponents add that the benefits would be concentrated mainly among taxpayers with higher incomes, while they would be modest for the middle class. This is an indication of how the benefits would be distributed, not a quantification: the text provides no percentages, amounts by income bracket or examples of individual tax returns. The committee's claim therefore remains tied to the comparison between the categories cited in the source, namely married and unmarried couples, taxpayers with higher incomes and the middle class.
### The estimate for the Confederation As regards public revenue, the committee points to a loss of revenue for the Confederation. The figures presented by the opponents are based on estimates by the Federal Tax Administration, the FTA, and indicate a range between 700 million and 3 billion francs per year.
The difference between the two extremes is 2,3 billion francs per year: the calculation derives from the difference between 3 billion and 700 million, the only monetary values indicated for this effect. The source does not select a central amount and does not detail a breakdown by cantons, municipalities or individual families. The documented figure is therefore a broad estimate attributed to the opponents and based on the FTA's assessments, not an individual amount associated with the vote.
The two aspects of the criticism thus remain distinct: on the one hand, the committee disputes the possible return of a disadvantage for unmarried couples and considers the benefit for the middle class limited; on the other, it quantifies the Confederation's lost revenue. To follow the issue from the perspective of tax practice, the reference is tax return.

item.title: Securitas allegedly violated labor law thousands of times
item.description: About 20'000 alleged violations between 2023 and 2025 About 900 employees involved in Central Switzerland Shifts that are too long and rest periods
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Approximately 20'000 alleged violations between 2023 and 2025 - Approximately 900 employees involved in Central Switzerland - Shifts that are too long and rest periods that are too short - Securitas disputes the total and denies systematic violations
## Key facts - Company → Securitas - Area → Central Switzerland - Period → 2023-2025 - Alleged violations → about 20'000 - Employees involved → about 900 - Jobs listed → prisons, hospitals and asylum centers - Analysis → internal data examined by SRF Investigativ - Date → October 19, 2026, update 08:08
On October 19, 2026, an analysis of internal data conducted by SRF Investigativ reported approximately 20'000 alleged violations of labor law between 2023 and 2025. The count reportedly concerned about 900 Securitas employees in Central Switzerland.
According to the account, the main problems involved excessively long shifts and insufficient rest periods. The employees involved were reportedly assigned mainly to prisons, hospitals and asylum centers. For years, the Swiss security company allegedly made its staff work for too long and too often. The experts who spoke to SRF Investigativ described the situation as a systematic violation of labor law.
### The experts' assessments
> “This is an expression of systematic behavior,” Denis G. Humbert, a lawyer specializing in labor law, told SRF, urging the authorities to intervene.
Kurt Pärli, a law professor at the University of Basel, agreed with this interpretation. According to the report, the scale can no longer be explained by a planning error and goes far beyond that.
The first aspect to distinguish is the numerical scale indicated by the analysis: about 20'000 alleged violations and about 900 people involved. The second concerns the nature of the allegations, which focused on shifts and rest periods. The source does not provide a breakdown by individual employee or by individual facility. The fact that the figure is associated with Central Switzerland delineates the geographical scope referred to by the analysis, which is not presented as a count relating to other areas. ## Data, assessments and company response
The most significant aspect of the case is not just the figure cited by SRF Investigativ, but the gap between three different levels: the analysis of internal data, the experts' assessment and Securitas's response. Keeping them separate makes it possible to correctly understand what is being contested and what the company acknowledges.
### The comparison between analysis and Securitas's response
| Aspect | Reported analysis and assessments | Securitas's statement | |---|---|---| | Count | Approximately 20'000 alleged violations between 2023 and 2025 | The company does not understand the overall number and does not rule out errors | | Nature | Experts speak of systematic violations | Securitas denies overall and systematic violations | | Practice | Shifts that are too long and rest periods that are too short | Securitas admits that part of the practice was not in line with the principles of labor law and internal values | | Trend | The text does not report a numerical series | The measures adopted are said to have reduced violations in recent years |
The comparison shows that the admission of partial non-compliance does not coincide with acceptance of the overall count. Securitas acknowledges that part of the practice did not comply with the principles of labor law and internal values, but disputes both the figure of approximately 20'000 violations and the characterization of the violations as overall and systematic.
The two main figures also describe different quantities. The approximately 20'000 alleged violations represent the disputed phenomenon, while the approximately 900 employees indicate the people who would have been involved. The text does not make it possible to establish how many violations were associated with each employee, nor whether they all worked in the same places or faced the same shifts.
The same caution applies to the areas indicated. The source cites prisons, hospitals and asylum centers as places where the employees would have been deployed in particular; it does not present that list as a complete breakdown of Securitas's activities. The data therefore make it possible to link the dispute to those three areas, but not to automatically extend it to every facility or site of the company.
The documented picture therefore remains a comparison between an internal analysis, professional assessments and a company response. The source does not report a definitive finding by the authorities that resolves the divergence between these positions. ## What remains documented and what remains open
### A limited admission, not an agreement on the count
In its written response to SRF, Securitas admitted that part of the practice did not comply with the principles of labor law and its own internal values. According to the company, the measures adopted would have helped reduce violations in recent years.
The same statement, however, contains a clear dispute over the overall figure. Securitas says it is unable to understand the number of approximately 20'000 violations, does not rule out the presence of errors, and emphasizes that, overall, there would not have been systematic violations of labor law. The text thus brings together a partial admission and a rejection of the overall interpretation attributed to the analysis.
### The limits of the available picture
The source does not explain how the alleged violations were counted, how they were distributed across individual years, or which employees and facilities were associated with each episode. Nor does it indicate which specific provisions of labor law would have been violated, which thresholds the shifts would have exceeded, or how short the recovery periods would have been.
There is also no quantification of the decrease attributed to the measures adopted. Securitas speaks of a reduction in recent years, but the text provides neither before-and-after figures nor an indication of when the measures would have been implemented. It is therefore not possible to describe the development of the phenomenon with numbers on the basis of the material reported.

item.title: Inheritance and gift tax in the Canton of Zurich
item.description: Guide to inheritance and gift tax in the Canton of Zurich: rates based on degree of kinship, exemptions for spouse and descendants, and compliance
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Zurich handles inheritances and gifts at the cantonal level - Tax rates are interpreted according to degree of kinship - Spouse and descendants fall under the indicated exemptions - Filing and deadlines are part of the analysis
## Key facts - Scope → inheritance and gift tax - Territory → Canton of Zurich - Criterion → degree of kinship - Exemptions → spouse and descendants - Requirements → declaration and deadlines to be observed
In the Canton of Zurich, inheritance and gift tax should be understood as a cantonal levy. The central point is to identify the degree of kinship relevant to the rate and verify whether the case falls within the exemptions indicated for spouses and descendants.
The source distinguishes this tax from two federal levies. Switzerland does not levy a federal inheritance and gift tax; direct federal tax and VAT are separate levies and not components of Zurich inheritance tax. Therefore, a cantonal percentage must not be presented as a sum of direct federal tax, VAT and a municipal share.
### The correct scope of the calculation
The areas of responsibility are not interchangeable. AFC/ESTV is associated with direct federal tax and VAT, while cantonal administrations concern cantonal and municipal taxation. UFAS/BSV oversees social security, including AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG, and does not set tax rates. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not determine the rates.
In the Zurich case, this map helps avoid a misdirected search. The reference remains the cantonal rules governing the levy. The municipal tax multiplier for ordinary taxes must not be added to the inheritance or gift tax calculation. Nor does the general principle that each Canton has its own law and multiplier authorize automatically including the municipal component in this calculation.
A table or calculation that presents the federal, cantonal and municipal levels together therefore risks describing a tax different from the one addressed by the source. Separating the levels is the starting point.
Kinship is the filter indicated by the source. The analysis must distinguish the family relationship and the corresponding tax category, without substituting one degree for another. Spouses and descendants are mentioned among the exempt cases; for other relationships, the criterion of degree of kinship remains to be followed.
The verification also concerns the form of compliance. The source refers to the declaration and deadlines to be observed: the rate alone does not exhaust the procedure. Anyone dealing with an inheritance or gift in the Canton of Zurich must therefore keep three levels distinct: the type of transaction, the relationship and compliance with the cantonal requirements. ## The comparison that matters: kinship
The term tax rates, by itself, is not enough to interpret an inheritance or a gift in the Canton of Zurich. The benchmark indicated by the source is the degree of kinship: the first question is not which tax level to add, but which category corresponds to the family relationship. Only then is any exemption checked, and the filing and deadlines arranged.
| Checkpoint | Practical reading | |---|---| | Operation | inheritance or gift | | Level | Zurich cantonal tax | | Criterion | degree of kinship | | Referenced exemptions | spouse and descendants | | Items not to add | direct federal tax, VAT and the municipal multiplier for ordinary taxes |
This sequence avoids two misleading comparisons. The first is turning cantonal tax into a combination of direct federal tax, VAT and a municipal share. The second is using a tax rate tied to a degree of kinship different from the actual one. A calculation must not round a percentage or convert it into an amount without an explicit basis.
### Three hypothetical scenarios
In the first scenario, the transfer concerns a spouse or a descendant. The check starts with the exemption indicated by the source; a generic percentage is not automatically substituted for it. The transaction still has to be placed within the filing process and the deadlines to be met.
In the second scenario, the relationship falls under another degree of kinship. The procedure's entry point changes: the corresponding category is sought, without transferring the exemption referenced for spouse and descendants. The source does not authorize treating all recipients in the same way.
In the third scenario, the search is directed to the wrong institution. AFC/ESTV concerns direct federal tax and VAT; UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG; UST/BFS concerns statistics. None of these references replaces the jurisdiction of the cantonal administrations for cantonal and municipal taxation. The useful check is therefore institutional before it is arithmetic.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the operational consequence is simple: a national framework does not erase differences between Cantons. Each Canton has its own law and multiplier, but in the case examined here, the municipal multiplier for ordinary taxes is not added. The reading must remain anchored to Zurich cantonal tax, the degree of kinship and the indicated exemptions. ## From reading to filing
To turn the rule into a practical check, it is advisable to proceed without skipping steps. The goal is not to create a national formula, but to keep the qualification of the transaction, the tax rate, and the filing obligation separate.
### Five practical steps
1. **Define the transaction.** Establish whether it is an inheritance or a gift. Both cases fall within the scope of Zurich's cantonal tax and must be identified before looking for the tax rate.
2. Identify the relationship. Place the relationship between the persons involved in the relevant degree of kinship. This is the benchmark indicated by the source and prevents applying a category different from the actual one.
3. Check the exemption. First verify whether the case concerns a spouse or descendants, for whom the source refers to an exemption. This indication should not automatically be extended to other relationships.
4. Isolate the tax level. Treat the tax as cantonal. The municipal multiplier for ordinary taxes must not be added; neither direct federal tax nor VAT are components of Zurich inheritance tax. The percentage must not be converted into an amount without an explicit basis.
5. Manage filing and deadlines. Once the qualification is complete, deal with the filing and comply with the prescribed deadlines. The operational point of reference is the cantonal administrations, not AFC/ESTV, which deals with IFD and VAT, nor UFAS/BSV or UST/BFS, respectively responsible for social security and statistics.
### Final check
Before closing the procedure, the check must answer three questions: was the transaction correctly qualified, is the degree of kinship the right one, and was any exemption considered without adding extraneous items? If one answer is missing, the calculation is not yet ready. The same check must include the compliance obligations, because the source expressly refers to the declaration and deadlines.
For the operational phase, consult dichiarazione delle imposte.

item.title: More Young Swiss women earn less despite being more educated
item.description: Born in 1995: income gap of 14% Born in 1965: income gap of 55% In 2025: tertiary education at 54% versus 48% Among parents
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Born in 1995: income gap of 14% - Born in 1965: income gap of 55% - In 2025: tertiary education at 54% versus 48% - Among parents, the gap remains at 51%
## Key facts - 1995 cohort → income gap: 14% - 1965 cohort → income gap: 55% - Weekly hours → from 17 hours to fewer than four - Standardized hourly pay → from almost 20% to less than 5% - Young women with tertiary qualifications in 2025 → 54% - Young men with tertiary qualifications in 2025 → 48% - Women without children → from 27% to 7% - Gap between parents → 51%
The 14% remains the gap between the overall labor incomes of women and men born in 1995. The figure shows that young women’s educational advantage has not yet translated into full economic equality.
The study, carried out by the University of Lausanne and the Swiss Foundation for Research in Social Sciences Fors, was published in the journal «Social Change in Switzerland» and is based on the analysis conducted by Daniel Oesch and Oliver Lipps of data from more than 215’000 people between the ages of 25 and 34, drawn from the Swiss labor force surveys conducted from 1991 to 2024.
### A reduced gap between generations
In the press release devoted to the research, the authors describe the trend as a «race to catch up». Among people born in 1965, women’s overall labor income was 55% lower than men’s. For those born in 1995, the difference fell to 14%.
The narrowing gap also concerns the labor market and working hours. The difference between the hours worked in a week fell from 17 hours to fewer than four. When standardized hourly pay is considered instead, the gap fell from almost 20% to less than 5%.
The study identifies education as one of the key factors. In 2025, 54% of young women in Switzerland held a tertiary qualification, that is, a university degree, a degree from a university of applied sciences or a higher vocational qualification. Among young men, the share was 48%. Women are also moving into professions with higher earning potential.
The reduction is reflected in comparisons with France, Sweden, Great Britain and the United States. For those born in 1965, Switzerland had the second-largest income gap among these countries; for the 1995 cohort, the smallest. Motherhood remains a dividing line: among women without children, the gap fell from 27% to 7%, while among parents it remained at 51%. ## What the numbers really show
### Three different measures of the same gap
Research does not use a single indicator. Overall labor income captures the economic distance between women and men; weekly hours show how much the two patterns of labor-force participation have converged; standardized hourly pay, on the other hand, makes it possible to observe the gap related to hourly pay.
This distinction changes how the results are read. For the generation born in 1995, the gap in overall income is 14%, while that in standardized hourly pay is less than 5%. The two percentages therefore describe different dimensions and should not be used as though they were the same measure. The shift from 17 hours to fewer than four also signals that the gap in weekly hours has narrowed, without eliminating every difference in total income.
| Indicator | Born in 1965 | Born in 1995 | |---|---:|---:| | Overall labor income | 55% | 14% | | Difference in weekly hours | 17 hours | fewer than four hours | | Standardized hourly pay | almost 20% | less than 5% |
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the education data add a second point of comparison. In 2025, 54% of young women had a tertiary qualification, compared with 48% of young men. The greater presence of women in university programs, universities of applied sciences, and higher vocational education coincides with progress toward professions with higher earning potential. The study presents this change as one of the key factors behind the catch-up, not as the automatic elimination of the gap.
### Family is the decisive turning point
The difference between women without children and parents makes it impossible to read the result as a single value for all stages of life. Among women without children, the gap fell from 27% to 7%. Among parents, by contrast, it has narrowed but remains at 51%. Motherhood is thus identified as an important dividing line, because after starting a family, the income gap widens considerably.
The international comparison also reinforces the significance of the change: Switzerland moves from having the second-largest gap for the 1965 generation to having the smallest gap for the 1995 cohort, considering France, Sweden, Great Britain, and the United States. ## How to use data for a personal comparison
The study provides a framework by generation, education and family situation. To read it without automatically attributing the result for an entire cohort to a single person, it is helpful to follow a simple sequence.
### Five steps to avoid confusing the measures
1. Identify the age comparison. The 14% figure concerns people born in 1995, while the 55% figure concerns those born in 1965. These are two generations observed in the study, not two proportions that can be applied indiscriminately.
2. Separate overall employment income from standardized hourly pay. The first comparison indicates a 14% gap for those born in 1995; the second falls to less than 5%. Using only one of the two measures would change the question being answered.
3. Consider weekly hours alongside them. The difference has fallen from 17 hours to fewer than four. This figure should be kept separate from hourly pay and overall income.
4. Add the level of education. In 2025, a tertiary qualification applied to 54% of young women and 48% of young men. The comparison includes universities, universities of applied sciences and higher vocational education.
5. Consider the family situation. The gap between women without children fell from 27% to 7%, while among parents it remains at 51%. The difference therefore changes when moving from the general comparison to one linked to family.
This step-by-step reading avoids turning 14% into a description that applies to every working woman or confusing the hourly gap with the gap in overall income. It also makes it possible to connect the figures to the trajectory identified by the researchers: a recovery across generations, accompanied by a still-clear gap after starting a family.
To compare your own income with the different figures appearing in the study, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte
*Source: [tvsvizzera.it](https://www.tvsvizzera.it/tvs/lavoro-ed-economia/le-giovani-guadagnano-meno-nonostante-maggiore-istruzione/92206648)*

## TL;DR - The Switzerland-EU package was submitted on March 13, 2026 - On November 29, 2026, there will be a vote on the supplementary financing of the AVS - Guy Parmelin has announced his resignation effective December 31, 2026
## Key facts - Switzerland-EU package → submitted to Parliament on March 13, 2026 - Vote → November 29, 2026 - Voting topics → AVS, fireworks, taxation of married couples, War Materiel Act - Consultation → strengthening political rights - Legislative proposal → platforms and youth protection
On March 13, 2026, the Federal Council submitted the Switzerland-EU package to Parliament. Switzerland and the EU negotiated it with the aim of stabilizing and developing bilateral relations. The Swiss Government's official portal page therefore identifies a precise institutional step: the package was sent to Parliament. However, the individual agreements making it up are not detailed.
### The political calendar indicated by the portal
On November 29, 2026, Swiss citizens will be called upon to vote on four issues: in addition to the additional financing of AVS, these include the taxation of married couples, the initiative concerning fireworks, and the War Materiel Act. The update provides the date and list of issues, but not a result. To read the news correctly, it is therefore necessary to distinguish the electoral date from a decision already taken.
Among the other updates, the Federal Council is finalizing its legislative proposal on platforms, intended to strengthen the protection of young people. The available text indicates the purpose and proposal status, without adding other operational details. The source does not specify, for example, the content of the measures or a deadline linked to the process.
The consultation on strengthening political rights concerns the participation of people with an intellectual disability. The stated objective is to enable full participation in political life and overcome their systematic exclusion from the right to vote at the federal level. This update too is presented as a consultation, not as a final outcome.
### Succession to the Federal Council
Guy Parmelin, President of the Confederation, announced his resignation from the Federal Council, scheduled for December 31, 2026. The successor will be elected by Parliament in the next session. The portal also associates the announcement with a press conference. The available information thus distinguishes the announcement, the date of resignation, and the subsequent parliamentary election. The page is part of the broader function of the official website, which publishes updates on the decisions and activities of the Federal Council, how it operates as a collegial body, and popular votes. ## The stage of a dossier changes how it is read
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the page's practical usefulness lies in distinguishing the stage each dossier is at. The portal brings together topics that do not have the same status: a negotiated package submitted to Parliament is not described as a decision that has already been implemented; a legislative proposal is not the same as an operational rule; a consultation is not equivalent to an outcome; a voting date does not anticipate the result.
| Dossier | Indicated status | Possible reading | |---|---|---| | Switzerland-EU package | Negotiated and submitted to Parliament | Objective: stabilize and develop bilateral relations | | Platforms | Completed legislative proposal | Objective: strengthen youth protection | | Political rights | Consultation | Objective: full participation of people with an intellectual disability | | Vote on November 29, 2026 | Four topics listed | Date and items, not the result | | Guy Parmelin's resignation | Announcement for December 31, 2026 | Successor elected by Parliament in the next session |
### What the text allows you to verify
The reference to the supplementary financing of the AVS identifies a specific topic, but does not allow any change to be calculated: the source does not indicate amounts or other financial details. The same applies to the taxation of married couples, the initiative on fireworks, and the law on war materiel. The four topics are listed as items on the ballot, without a description of the individual measures.
The Switzerland-EU package, too, should be read without jumping ahead. The portal indicates the objective of bilateral relations and the submission to Parliament, but does not describe any further practical effects. The consultation on political rights signals a clear direction, namely full participation by people with an intellectual disability, without presenting an outcome. The proposal on platforms identifies youth protection as its aim, without turning the title into an already defined rule.
For the reader, the result is a reliability map: the voting date is a scheduled event, the submission reflects the package's status, the consultation is a phase of discussion, the proposal is a text under development, and the resignation is an announcement with a date. Sticking to these definitions allows the federal agenda to be followed without adding consequences that the source does not set out. ## From the portal to the operational reminder
The safest way to use the update is to turn it into a status reminder, not a list of consequences that are not indicated. The official website of the Swiss Government provides updates on the decisions and activities of the Federal Council, on its work as a collegial body, and on popular votes. For those who want to follow the dossiers, this function makes it possible to record dates, stage and subject without confusing a proposal with an outcome.
### Five practical checks
1. Record the submission. Next to the Switzerland-EU package, note March 13, 2026 and Parliament. The note to retain is that the package was negotiated to stabilize and develop bilateral relations.
2. Separate the voting topics. For November 29, 2026, list the four items on four separate lines: additional funding for AVS, an initiative concerning fireworks, the taxation of spouses and the War Material Act. The date is the same, but the items remain separate.
3. Indicate the stage of the proposal concerning platforms. The Federal Council is completing the bill to strengthen youth protection. The reminder should include this objective, without adding measures or deadlines that are not indicated.
4. Keep the consultation on political rights separate. The item concerns people with an intellectual disability and the goal of full participation in political life, without treating it as an already announced result.
5. Follow the resignation schedule. For Guy Parmelin, note December 31, 2026, and keep separate the subsequent election of the successor by Parliament during the next session. The page also indicates a statement linked to a press conference.
The final check consists of maintaining the same precision used by the portal: proposal, consultation, submission, announcement and vote are different words and describe different steps. The source does not provide amounts, results or detailed content of the individual measures; therefore, the update is intended to schedule and follow the dossiers, not to calculate effects that the text does not present. item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Topic: apprenticeship in the Canton of Zurich - Focus: position, contract and remuneration - Pathway: vocational baccalaureate
## Key facts - Territory → Canton of Zurich - Subject → apprenticeship and vocational education and training - Checks → position, contract, remuneration, vocational baccalaureate
The Canton of Zurich is the scope of the in-depth analysis devoted to apprenticeships and vocational education and training. The editorial angle starts from four concrete questions: how to find an apprenticeship position, what to check in the apprenticeship contract, how to read an apprentice's remuneration and how to understand the vocational baccalaureate. It is an evergreen article: not a chronicle of a decision, but a practical map for navigating the Swiss system without filling gaps with figures that are not provided.
### The scope of the guide
The first step is to separate the four areas. The apprenticeship position concerns finding the opportunity; the contract concerns the conditions to read before committing; remuneration concerns the relationship between the agreed amount and deductions; the vocational baccalaureate concerns the educational path to be checked with the competent authority. The source does not provide a standard amount for the apprentice, nor a list of companies, deadlines or requirements specific to the Canton of Zurich. Therefore, the missing data cannot be replaced with a national figure or an invented rule.
The reference point remains the general framework for employment in Switzerland. There is no federal minimum wage; some Cantons have their own. For working hours, the maximum limit indicated is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and retail, or 50 hours in other sectors. The minimum vacation entitlement is four weeks, five for those under 20. These are references to compare with the contract and applicable rules, not an automatic wage.
### Salary is not just the figure
Contributions come into play in pay: AVS/AHV, AI and IPG are borne by the employee at 5,3%, while the total with the employer is 10,6%; AD/AC is 1,1% up to the annual maximum. LAINF/LAA varies from 0,7% to 1,5% depending on the sector. For LPP/BVG on the coordinated salary, the source indicates rates of 7% between 25 and 34 years, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from age 55 up to the reference age.
These data explain why the right question is not only how much an apprentice earns, but what amount is provided for and what items accompany it. To begin the search, you can consult the annunci di lavoro, keeping the offer, the contract and the school pathway separate. The practical assessment of an apprenticeship in the Canton of Zurich cannot be based on a predetermined national amount. The source clarifies that there is no federal minimum wage and that some cantons have their own rules. The comparison must therefore remain anchored to the individual offer, the apprenticeship contract and the items affecting disposable income.
### From pay to monthly budget
The remuneration figure indicated is not the whole calculation. Social contributions are linked to salary, whereas LAMal/KVG follows a different logic: for residents, it is compulsory private health insurance with per-capita premiums. It is neither a tax nor a salary contribution. Premiums vary by canton and region, and premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy.
For an adult, the deductibles indicated are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500. Even without entering an invented amount for remuneration, these items make it possible to carry out an orderly assessment of the cost of living: first consider the amount specified in the contract, then separate out social deductions and finally add the health insurance premium. The result is not a national rate, but a personal budget linked to the specific situation.
| Item | Practical interpretation | |---|---| | Remuneration | It should be compared with what is stated in the offer or contract. | | Contributions | They are deductions linked to salary and applicable rules. | | LAMal/KVG | It is separate from the payslip and has per-capita premiums. | | Cantonal rules | Requirements, deadlines and amounts must be verified with the competent canton. |
### Scenarios to keep separate
In a hypothetical scenario, a resident who comes to Switzerland to begin a training program must take out health insurance within three months of arrival. The deadline concerns LAMal, not the signing of the apprenticeship contract. Confusing the two procedures leads to looking for the deadline at the wrong office.
In another hypothetical scenario, age changes how vacation is interpreted: the stated minimum is four weeks, which becomes five for anyone under 20. LPP/BVG is also presented by age brackets based on the coordinated salary. It is therefore not advisable to infer a deduction solely from the fact that the person is an apprentice.
To read a Swiss payslip correctly, the individual items can be examined in the guide to busta paga svizzera. The point is always to distinguish between salary, contributions and cost of living: they are three related but non-interchangeable aspects. The safest procedure is to turn the search for an apprenticeship into a checklist, without attributing to the Canton of Zurich requirements or amounts that the source does not indicate.
### Four operational steps
1. Define the dossier. Write separately the objective of the apprenticeship position, the contract to be examined, the remuneration to be compared and any interest in the vocational baccalaureate. This division avoids treating training as a simple salary question.
2. Search for the opportunity and keep the offer. When you find a position, note the proposed amount, working hours, vacation and every item related to pay. If an element is unclear, ask for an answer referring to the specific case instead of using a national average.
3. Verify which level is responsible. For requirements, deadlines and amounts linked to cantonal services, consult the official source of the Canton. The same criterion applies to any contributions to continuing education and to programs that depend on the canton, municipality or competent institution. For the vocational baccalaureate, the source indicates the topic but does not provide conditions or deadlines: these must be requested from the competent authority.
4. Reconstruct the budget. Start from the expected remuneration and separate social deductions from the LAMal/KVG premium. If the person is resident and arrives in Switzerland, consider the three-month deadline for taking out health insurance. Do not enter precise amounts when the year is not certain: the source notes that the average LAMal premiums, the threshold and coordination deduction under LPP, and the AD/AC maximum are indexed annually.
### Finding the right office
The choice of contact person also matters. AFC/ESTV concerns direct federal tax and VAT; cantonal administrations manage cantonal and municipal taxation. UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS, AI and LPP, but does not set tax rates. UST/BFS produces statistics and does not establish rates. Separating these roles reduces the risk of using an official page for a question that belongs to another authority.
For a final check of the budget related to training, income and current expenses, consult costo della vita in Svizzera.

## TL;DR - In Thun, the SP supported three popular initiatives - Baume-Schneider spoke about financing the 13th AVS pension - The SP is calling for shorter working hours and higher wages - Referendum against the Mercosur agreement approved
## Key facts - Location → Thun (BE) - Duration → two-day congress - Initiatives → mobility voucher, bees and internet - Estimated monthly burden → around 15 francs for an average household - Document → “Decent work for everyone!”
### The congress and the decisions Thun (BE) hosted the PS’s two-day congress, which concluded with official support for three popular initiatives. On the second day, the Socialists put forward proposals concerning transport, pollination and the responsibility of digital platforms.
The previous day, the congress had reached its climax with the launch of the Initiative for the protection of women against violence. The final day, by contrast, focused on the three initiatives supported by the party. The first concerns the mobility voucher: the aim is to promote Swiss public transport and rail links with neighboring countries.
The second is the bee initiative. It calls on the Confederation and cantons to ensure the pollination of cultivated and wild plants by bees, making the necessary resources available. The third concerns the internet and seeks to require platforms, including search engines and artificial-intelligence developers, to assess the risks associated with the services they offer and adopt measures to contain them.
Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider also addressed the delegates. She spoke about financing the 13th AVS/AHV pension and warned that, without an additional contribution, the AVS would already record a negative result this year, triggering a downward spiral. To finance the expenditure, the increase in VAT would mean an additional burden of around 15 francs a month for an average household.
Baume-Schneider, from Jura, praised the PS’s strength for the community and its willingness to change power relations. She also described the heatwaves and persistent drought as worrying, identifying them as symptoms of climate change.
The congress also approved the policy document “Decent work for everyone!”, calling for shorter working hours, higher wages and greater participation in decision-making. The delegates, however, rejected the bill aimed at abolishing cantonal and municipal minimum wages. The referendum against the bill was launched by the PS together with the trade unions and other organizations. Co-president Cédric Wermuth described it as:
> Cédric Wermuth described the project as a threat to workers’ purchasing power and an affront to democracy and federalism.
Finally, the party supported the referendum aimed at opposing the free-trade agreement with the Mercosur countries. Mattea Meyer, co-president, lamented the lack of effective measures against deforestation and forced labor. ## What it means for families and workers
### The tax figure should be read as a scenario The reference to around 15 francs per month is the most concrete point for a household. Baume-Schneider links it to a VAT increase needed to cover the cost of the 13th AVS/AHV pension, but the source gives neither a rate nor a date nor a step that has already been completed. The figure therefore describes a political scenario presented at the congress, not an amount the reader should already enter as a charge.
This distinction also helps from a tax perspective: this concerns VAT, not direct federal tax. To assess the possible impact on the cost of living without overstating it, it is useful to separate the monthly estimate from the decisions still to be made. The source does not make it possible to calculate a different burden by canton, income, or household composition, because it does not provide these details.
### Wages and rules still to be defined The labor document outlines three directions, but does not establish a wage amount, new working hours, or a timetable. For an employee, this means that the news does not provide enough to infer a change in their payslip. The section on minimum wages, however, has a specific local dimension: the contested proposal aims to dismantle cantonal and municipal minimum wages, while the referendum launched by the SP, trade unions, and other organizations opens the debate over that decision. The source does not report its outcome.
The other initiatives should likewise be read as goals, not as effects that can already be measured. The mobility voucher is not accompanied by any amounts or a new rail service; the proposal concerning bees calls for resources, but does not quantify the resources needed; the text on the internet does not specify checks or sanctions. The referendum on Mercosur is linked to measures against deforestation and forced labor, but the report does not describe the content of the agreement or the outcome of the vote.
To relate the estimate to the household budget, one can consult costo della vita in Svizzera, keeping the published data and political assumptions separate. ## How to follow the dossiers
### Four practical steps The source provides a reading checklist, but not a complete administrative procedure. To avoid confusing political support, referendums and concrete implementation, proceed as follows.
1. Identify the precise proposal. Mobility, bees and the internet are not the same dossier: associate each with its objective and do not attribute to one proposal measures intended for another.
2. If you are assessing the family budget, record the approximately 15 francs per month only as an estimate linked to the VAT increase described by Baume-Schneider. Do not use them as an amount already collected, and keep this figure separate from any calculation concerning direct federal tax.
3. For work, keep the policy document on wages and working hours distinct from the referendum against the bill on cantonal and municipal minimum wages. You can compare the political demands with your busta paga svizzera, without automatically considering them new applicable rules.
4. For initiatives and referendums, note only the information provided: the source does not indicate voting dates, deadlines, VAT rates, entry into force or documents to be filed. Any operational schedule added to this news item would be invented.
The Mercosur dossier should be followed separately, because it concerns a free trade agreement and measures against deforestation and forced labor. The reference to heat waves and drought also remains, in the source, an assessment by the federal councillor concerning climate change: it contains no procedure or deadline for readers.

item.title: Covid allowance abuses hit hundreds of firms
item.description: 7'200 companies verified out of more than 167'000 beneficiaries SECO reclaimed 243,53 million in ILR Lastminute returned 28,9 million in Ticino
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 7'200 companies audited out of more than 167'000 recipient companies - SECO claimed 243,53 million in ILR - Lastminute repaid 28,9 million in Ticino - At the end of December 2025, 133,7 million remained outstanding
## Key facts - Companies checked → 7'200 - Total benefits → more than 16 billion francs - Recoveries claimed by SECO → 243,53 million - Lastminute in Ticino → 28,9 million repaid - Evident abuses → 171 checks - Unintentional errors → approximately 1'200 companies
### The scope of the checks 7'200 companies were subjected to review by the Confederation as part of checks into suspected abuses of short-time work compensation (ILR) paid during the coronavirus pandemic. The review covered a total of more than 167'000 companies which, overall, received more than 16 billion francs.
The State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) has completed the checks and, according to the assessment reported by SonntagsBlick, considered the result positive. The formula used to describe it is this:
> «For every franc paid out, it was possible to claim back eight francs».
As of last October 2, SECO's checks had led to claims for 243,53 million francs in ILR. The checks entrusted to external auditors had cost 31,36 million. The Sunday paper, however, pointed out two caveats: the calculations would not include internal costs, and the word «claim» does not mean that the money has already been received.
The recovery, in fact, does not take place directly through SECO. The unemployment funds collect it and, through their own investigations, claimed another 430 million. Adding the two amounts, the total claim reaches 680 million; at the end of December 2025, 133,7 million were still outstanding. The newspaper specifies that no more recent data are available.
One particularly significant case concerns Lastminute, an online travel operator active in Ticino, forced to repay 28,9 million. In 171 checks, SECO gathered evidence of «evident abuses» and referred each case to the competent cantonal prosecutors' offices. For approximately 1'200 companies, by contrast, the auditors attributed the irregularities to unintentional errors. ## What the figures indicate
The practical point for a company, public body or reader is to distinguish the entity that conducts the checks from the one that recovers the money. SECO verified the cases and quantified some of the claims; the unemployment funds conducted their own investigations and claimed additional amounts. To interpret a dispute or a set of accounts, adding the figures without indicating the source creates an incomplete picture: the total of 680 million is not presented as a sum that has already been collected in full.
### Three levels not to be confused
| Item | What it indicates | |---|---| | Claimed | A claimed receivable, not necessarily collected | | Received | The money actually collected; the source does not quantify it | | Outstanding | Part of the receivable still to be recovered at the end of December 2025 |
This distinction changes how the impact on the unemployment insurance accounts is understood. The amounts claimed show the size of the claims; the amounts received would measure the actual recovery. The source notes that the second figure is not available for the amount attributed to SECO and that, in the overall picture, a portion remained outstanding at the end of 2025.
The relationship between checks and irregularities also calls for caution. The 171 cases involving clear abuses concern audits in which, according to SECO, there was evidence. These findings cannot be placed on the same footing as the approximately 1'200 cases classified as unintentional errors. The distinction matters for the companies involved: in the source, intentional fraud and error are not equivalent categories.
Geographically and by sector, Lanzeray rules out any particular concentration: according to his statement, the propensity for fraud would not depend on a specific industry or region. Therefore, the Lastminute case in Ticino is relevant because of the amount repaid, but the source does not present it as evidence of an anomaly specific to the canton.
The cost of external auditors adds another angle. The 31,36 million cited do not include, according to the Sunday paper, internal costs. Comparing this with the amount claimed is therefore not enough to describe a final net balance. For anyone following the case, the right question is not simply how much money was claimed: one must ask which investigation the amounts belong to, what date they refer to and whether they are described as receivables or collections. The same figure changes meaning if it concerns an outstanding claim or a repayment that has already taken place. ## How to verify a figure on ILR
For a reader who needs to check a piece of news, or for a company that wants to understand how to read a dispute, the safest approach is to separate the steps. This is a reading framework built on the available data, not a legal procedure.
1. **Identify the body.** Note whether the amount is attributed to SECO or to unemployment funds: the two entries derive from different checks.
2. Fix the date. For SECO data, the reference is last October 2; for amounts still outstanding, the snapshot is as of the end of December 2025.
3. Read the verb. To claim indicates a request for repayment; the source warns that this does not automatically mean a payment was received.
4. Separate the outcomes. Clear-cut abuse backed by evidence must be kept distinct from an involuntary error. In the former cases, SECO filed complaints with the competent cantonal prosecutors' offices.
5. Check the scope. A single case should not be used to attribute a propensity for fraud to a sector or region: Lanzeray does not identify any particular concentrations.
### Where the source stops
This method avoids the first reading error: turning a request into a payment received. It also avoids confusing a check with the outcome of a complaint. The article reports that, in cases of clear-cut abuse, the cantonal prosecutors' offices received complaints; however, it does not describe what happened next in the proceedings.
For a single company, then, the point to establish is the nature of the outcome: clear-cut abuse with evidence or involuntary error. The source does not indicate forms, documents, deadlines or procedures for challenging a request, so these elements cannot be inferred from the overall results of the checks alone.
Anyone assessing the recovery of benefits should also keep the subject, date, verb and status of the amount separate. The reference to the most recent data remains what the newspaper stated: they are not available. Until an item is merely claimed, the headline does not amount to a completed recovery.

item.title: FFS: 97 heat-related track deformations, task force for summer 2026
item.description: The FFS recorded 97 deformations and crushings.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The FFS recorded 97 cases of deformation and buckling. - The figure is almost four times that of the previous year. - A task force has been established for summer 2026. - The white paint lost half its effect after two years.
## Key facts - Cases: 97 deformations and crushing - Comparison: almost four times the previous year - Task force: set up for the heat of summer 2026 - Monitoring: dense SBB network - White paint: initial effect of about 4.5 degrees
### The data communicated by the SBB In the response to Keystone-ATS, the SBB endorsed the data of 97 deformations and crushing of the tracks, cited by the SonntagsZeitung. The communication, dated Bern, concerns last summer, marked by exceptional temperatures. According to Sunday, the figure is almost four times higher than that recorded in the previous year.
The phenomenon includes deformations and expansions of the railway infrastructure. The company said the increase had no impact on safety. In the same newspaper, however, Patrick Braess, an expert at the Federal Polytechnic University of Zurich, warned of the risk of derailments caused by the heat.
SBB explained that it has a dense monitoring network. Events with safety implications are systematically transmitted to the Federal Office of Transport. The rails are regularly checked with measuring and diagnostic vehicles, so as to assess the situation in a targeted manner. Rigorous infrastructure maintenance has been identified as the most important preventive measure. The company also pointed out that zero risk never exists.
Monitoring, reporting and vehicle checks are described as tools already used by SBB. The task force is instead in charge of defining any additional measures for exceptional heat, if necessary.
Faced with the exceptional heat of summer 2026, the company has set up a task force to define additional measures, if necessary. The strategy also includes long-term interventions: concrete sleepers, considered more stable than those in wood, and a higher neutralization temperature during welding, to make the rails more resistant to temperatures that tend to be higher.
SBB also experimented with white paint. At first, cooling averaged about 4.5 degrees; after two years, the dirt had reduced the effect to about half. The more intense the traffic, the faster the effect fades. This is why SBB is evaluating, in an ongoing analysis, whether white coatings are sensible in certain cases. ### An increase to be viewed with caution For those who live or work in Switzerland and use the train, the figure must be considered on two levels: the number of occurrences and their operational consequences. The source indicates 97 cases of deformation and buckling, but does not report delays, cancellations, speed restrictions or timetable changes. Consequently, that number alone does not make it possible to describe the punctuality of the services or the impact on a single line.
The second distinction concerns safety. The FFS state that the increase has no repercussions for safety; Patrick Braess, by contrast, points to the risk of derailment linked to heat. In the source, the two statements are not accompanied by a shared technical explanation. The relevant point for the reader is therefore the existence of a comparison: the company's assessment on the one hand, the expert's warning on the other. Neither position can be turned into a broader assessment than the one reported.
On a practical level, the FFS's response combines monitoring and infrastructure interventions. Measurement and diagnostic vehicles are used to assess the tracks in a targeted way; rigorous maintenance is identified as the main preventive measure. Concrete sleepers and raising the neutralization temperature during welding, on the other hand, are among the long-term solutions. The difference is significant: the first line of action identifies problems, while the second aims to make the tracks more stable or more heat-resistant.
The white paint also shows the limits of an apparently simple response. The initial cooling effect did not remain unchanged: dirt and heavy traffic reduced it. The FFS are therefore evaluating coatings in certain cases, without presenting them in the source as a general solution. For the public, this means that the issue remains technical and operational: no measure that applies equally to every route has been announced, but an analysis linked to track conditions. ### The verifiable operational sequence The source does not describe deadlines or procedures that passengers must follow. The concrete action reported concerns FFS and can be reconstructed into a precise sequence.
First step: regular inspection of the rails. Swiss Federal Railways use measurement and diagnostic vehicles to examine the infrastructure. This makes it possible to assess the situation in a targeted manner, as specified by the company.
Second step: monitoring and reporting. FFS have a dense monitoring network; when an event is relevant to safety, it is systematically reported to the Federal Office of Transport. The source does not indicate any other authorities or reporting channels, so it is not possible to add a different procedure.
Third step: maintenance. FFS define rigorous infrastructure maintenance as the most important preventive measure. This principle is accompanied by technical interventions: where provided for, concrete sleepers instead of wooden ones and a higher neutralization temperature during welding.
Fourth step: additional measures. The task force established for summer 2026 must define any further interventions if necessary. The source does not indicate a deadline or a definitive list of measures. White paint is also still under analysis: its cooling effect is reduced by dirt and fades more quickly when traffic is heavy.
The final point stated by FFS is that zero risk never exists. The task force and the analysis of coatings are therefore, in the source, tools for deciding whether to add measures, not announcements of an outcome that has already been determined.
For the reader, the actionable information is above all a distinction: the source does not ask anyone to change their travel behavior and does not announce a new rule for passengers. Instead, it describes how the company monitors, reports, maintains and assesses. To explore the topic of everyday mobility further, consult the guide to mezzi pubblici.
