item.description: ESA celebrates Prodex’s first 40 years Swiss and Belgian delegations launched Prodex in 1986 Zurich hosted the conference and ceremony In Switzerland
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - ESA celebrates Prodex's first 40 years - Swiss and Belgian delegations launched Prodex in 1986 - Zurich hosted the conference and ceremony - 130 projects funded in Switzerland over 40 years
## Key facts - Date → October 16, 2026 - Program → Prodex - Agency → ESA - Participation → 17 member states - Projects in Switzerland → 130 - University research centers → over 20 - Contributions to Swiss industry → over 50% - Celebrations → Zurich, from October 14 to 16, 2026
The press release of October 16, 2026, celebrates the first 40 years of Prodex, the European Space Agency (ESA) program dedicated to experimental space research. Since 1986, Prodex has provided resources for the development and use of scientific instruments and experiments.
Switzerland played a decisive role in the creation of Prodex and, through the program, finances its own space experiments. The program thus aims to support standards of scientific excellence in ESA missions and those of international partners such as NASA, JAXA and CNES.
### Why the program was created Space research is considered one of ESA's pillars. In general, the research institutes of member states develop the Agency's scientific experiments, while the respective states finance their implementation. States without their own national funding instrument therefore lacked an equivalent opportunity.
To address this need, in 1986, the Swiss and Belgian delegations launched Prodex, working with prominent figures from the scientific and administrative worlds. Currently, 17 member states of the Agency participate in the program.
ESA's experience enables Prodex to send highly complex scientific instruments and experiments into space, used both in the Agency's missions and those of international partners; these include the space agencies of the United States, Japan and France.
The anniversary was celebrated in Zurich from October 14 to 16, 2026, with a conference and a ceremony. The opening address was given by State Secretary Martina Hirayama. During several roundtable discussions, delegations from the participating states engaged with representatives of ESA and figures from the space research and industry communities.
Over the past 40 years, 130 development projects for space experiments have received support in Switzerland, carried out by more than 20 university research centers. Through specific mandates, more than 50% of the contributions were allocated to Swiss industry. The practical significance described by the source unfolds on two levels: the path that takes instruments into space and their subsequent use on Earth. With Prodex, highly complex scientific instruments and experiments can reach space and be used in ESA missions and those of partners such as NASA, JAXA and CNES.
### From mission to everyday life
| Field | What the source indicates | |---|---| | Research | Scientific instruments and experiments used in space missions | | Industry | More than 50% of contributions allocated to Swiss industry | | Exploration | Rosetta monitored a comet for several years | | Planets | CHEOPS precisely measures exoplanets | | Earth | Observation of the planet and climate, weather forecasts and alerts in the event of disasters |
The technological path starts with the development of instruments, passes through space missions and leads to technologies that can be refined and used for other missions, infrastructure and applications in everyday life on Earth. For Swiss citizens, the benefit cited is linked above all to Earth and climate observation, with results concerning weather forecasts and alerts in the event of disasters.
The examples illustrate the variety of results. Rosetta made it possible, for the first time, to monitor a comet for several years and make important discoveries about the origin of water on Earth. CHEOPS was ESA's first mission led by Switzerland and, at European level, the first to precisely measure exoplanets.
Thanks to Prodex, instruments and experiments were also developed for ESA's Euclid space telescope, NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and the International Space Station. The research described in the press release therefore extends from the exploration of comets and exoplanets to the observation of Earth.
The comparison before and after the program began concerns funding. States without a national instrument did not have a corresponding opportunity; after 1986, Prodex provides resources for the development and use of scientific instruments and experiments. Today, 17 Member States of the Agency participate in the program. To turn the press release into a practical reading, it is useful to use a five-step checklist. Each item can be linked directly to the elements indicated by the source, without adding external data.
### Five steps for finding one's bearings
1. Set the timeframe. Record the publication date, 16 October 2026, and the period of the celebrations, from 14 to 16 October 2026. The location is Zurich, where the conference and ceremony took place.
2. Identify the connection. Prodex is ESA's programme that promotes experimental space research and provides resources for the development and use of scientific instruments and experiments.
3. Follow the Swiss path. Note the role of the Swiss and Belgian delegations in its launch in 1986, then link the programme to the figure of 130 development projects funded in Switzerland and carried out by more than 20 university research centres.
4. Check where the contributions go. Record the share indicated for Swiss industry: over 50%, through dedicated mandates. This step distinguishes the industrial component from the university one.
5. Separate space and Earth. Alongside missions and telescopes, look for the section concerning Earth and climate observation. The source cites weather forecasts and alerts in the event of disasters as applications that also benefit Swiss citizens.
The institutional part of the event should be kept distinct from the scientific results. Martina Hirayama delivered the opening speech, while the round tables brought the delegations of the participating states, ESA representatives and figures from space research and industry together for discussion.
The last check consists in verifying that every example remains anchored to the source: Rosetta, CHEOPS, Euclid, James Webb or the International Space Station. Thus the reader recognizes the international dimension of the missions and the Swiss presence in research and industry, without attributing to the programme results other than those described.

item.title: Social assistance for Ukrainian refugees: mixed opinions
item.description: The cantons will be able to set the amount of social assistance S Next year, 46'000 refugees will be able to receive it Consultation on Ordinance 2
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Cantons will be able to set the amount of social assistance S - Next year, 46'000 refugees will be able to receive it - Consultation on Asylum Ordinance 2 until October 15 - Cantonal laws to be adjusted by March 1, 2027
## Key facts - Subject → amendment of Asylum Ordinance 2 - Beneficiaries → Ukrainian refugees with S status - Figure given → 46'000 people next year - Consultation → until October 15 - Deadline for cantonal laws → March 1, 2027 - 2027 relief package → global lump sum abolished for some S-status holders
BERN - The draft submitted for consultation on the amendment of Asylum Ordinance 2 provides for the cantons to determine the amount of social assistance intended for Ukrainian refugees benefiting from S status. The Confederation is reducing its financial commitment for cost-saving reasons and therefore intends to leave the task of setting benefits to the cantons, as they will bear the costs.
Starting next year, 46'000 Ukrainian refugees will be able to receive social assistance for the first time. The amendment, concerning the adjustment of Asylum Ordinance 2, was submitted for consultation until October 15.
### Why the ordinance is being amended
Mathias Reynard, president of the Conference of Cantonal Directors of Social Affairs, explained to Keystone-ATS that without the amendment, people with S status would receive the same social benefit as residents. The amount would therefore be higher than the amount currently in force for asylum seekers. This would result in a considerable increase in costs for the cantons.
The financial pressure has also increased as a result of another decision. The 2027 relief package abolished the global lump sum that the Confederation paid to the cantons for people with S status who held a residence permit for more than 5 years. The federal draft therefore forms part of a cost-sharing arrangement in which the Confederation's commitment is decreasing while the cantonal one is growing.
### Positions in the consultation
The cantons had asked to be able to determine the amount of benefits independently, and the draft accepted this request. In future, the amounts may be reduced to match those provided for asylum seekers.
The municipalities welcome the amendment but ask to have a say. The Association of Swiss Municipalities emphasizes that they bear the main financial burden. Humanitarian organizations, on the other hand, point to possible social consequences. The issue therefore remains open between cantonal autonomy, the transfer of costs and concerns about protecting people with S status. ## Three scenarios for the Cantons
The practical scope of the project emerges from a comparison of three outcomes already indicated in the consultation. The first is what would occur without an amendment: holders of S status would receive the same subsidy as residents, with an amount higher than that currently provided for asylum seekers. For the Cantons, the indicated consequence is a significant increase in costs.
| Scenario | Consequence indicated in the source | |---|---| | Ordinance not amended | Social assistance as for residents | | Ordinance amended | Cantons set even lower amounts | | Court appeal | Depending on the judgment, possible retroactive payment of the full amount of social assistance |
In the second scenario, decision-making discretion passes to the Cantons. Amounts may fall to the level of social assistance provided for asylum seekers. The difference is therefore not merely administrative: it can translate into different benefits depending on the cantonal decision. The project thus links the determination of the amount to the Cantons' ability to directly bear the associated cost.
### The legal and social risk
Potential litigation opens a third scenario. PS, OSAR, Caritas and Verdi fear poverty and unequal treatment before the law; they also point to obstacles to integration and participation in social life. A ruling could require the Cantons to pay the full amount of social assistance retroactively. The decision on the amount would thus have financial consequences even after its implementation.
The PLR focuses on the revision's compatibility with the Convention relating to the Status of Refugees and asks the Federal Council to clarify the legal issue. The UDC, by contrast, takes a cost-saving approach: it approves moving away from equivalence with benefits for Swiss citizens, but considers the savings potential in the asylum sector still untapped and calls for the project to be strengthened.
For municipalities and Cantons, the comparison therefore concerns two opposing risks: on the one hand, higher costs if the ordinance remains unchanged; on the other, litigation and possible back payments if the reduction does not withstand legal scrutiny. ## Following the dossier, step by step
The source indicates a useful sequence for understanding the change without confusing the levels of decision-making. First comes the federal consultation on Asylum Ordinance 2; then, if the amendment is adopted, the cantons will be able to set the amounts; finally, their social assistance laws will have to be adjusted by the deadline referred to by PLR. For municipalities, the request to participate in the decisions remains open, because they bear the main financial burden.
### Four operational steps
1. Until October 15, follow the consultation on the adjustment of Asylum Ordinance 2. This is the first deadline explicitly indicated in the source.
2. During the autumn, distinguish the political aspiration from the final decision: PLR is calling for the amendment to be adopted during this period, so as to leave the cantons time.
3. After any possible adoption, monitor the cantonal determination of the amount. The project provides that the cantons may set lower benefits, down to the level provided for asylum seekers.
4. By March 1, 2027, follow the adjustment of the cantonal social assistance laws, a deadline indicated by PLR to allow the cantons to complete the legislative work.
For a person with S status, the practically decisive factor will be the amount set by the competent canton. The source indicates that it could be reduced to the level of the benefit provided for asylum seekers. However, no single figure is reported: the comparison will therefore have to focus on the cantonal decision that follows any federal amendment.
For municipalities, the step to follow is the request to have a say in the decisions, since the Swiss Association of Municipalities attributes the main financial burden to them. For political parties and humanitarian organizations, the key issues remain compatibility with the Convention relating to the Status of Refugees, the risk of appeals, and the consequences for poverty, integration, and social participation.
Until these steps are completed, the operational data is not a definitive amount, but the transfer of authority envisaged by the project and the political timetable indicated in the source.
